history: Yangzhou rose with the Grand Canal — 'in misty March go down to Yangzhou', Li Bai's invitation. After Emperor Yang dug the canal it became a Tang world-city: 'Yang first, Yi second'. The five-pavilion bridge and white pagoda of Slender West Lake are picture-perfect; Ge Garden's four-season rocks are unique; Yangzhou fried rice and morning tea are known worldwide.
importance: Firstborn of the Canal · Famous city of Huai-Zuo
foods: Fried rice with ham and shrimp — born of state banquets.
Lion's-head meatballs stewed with crab roe — melts in the mouth.
Fuchun Teahouse's three-delicacy bun with Kuilongzhu tea.
Knife-cut dried tofu in chicken soup — fresh.
Tofu sliced into hairs — the supreme Huaiyang knife skill.
Morning tea starts with hot shredded tofu.
Lotus-root-powder skin with fruit filling — bouncy and smooth.
scenes: Willows and flowers along the water — Five-Pavilion Bridge and Twenty-Four Bridge.
Four-season rock gardens — the greatest salt-merchant garden.
'First garden of late Qing' — the double corridor.
Where Jianzhen set sail for Japan — the Qiling Pagoda.
Thousand-year old street — Xie Fuchun cosmetics and lacquerware.
